account:
Today has mostly looked like ordinary town business. The plaza townsfolk I asked had no news. The innkeeper reported eight fresh loaves, no lodging requests, and no town concerns; he was checking accommodation and clearing spoiled stock. The baker advertised fresh bread. Freight says he is checking the week's delivery schedule and offers warehouse and ferry services, but has identified no particular shipment or unusual activity to me.

The builder reported inspecting the bridge, bakery approach, east landing approach, and quay road. He found them passable, with no verified damage or immediate danger, though he explicitly did not provide structural certification. He seeks agreement on payment and any further inspection scope. I have commissioned neither further inspection nor cargo. His repeated requests seem consistent with arranging paid work, not evidence of a hidden undertaking.

The secretary is coordinating visitors and requests and holds the appointment book, which I saw them take from its chest this morning. Several of the secretary's remarks have been unintelligible to me, so I still lack a clear accounts summary and the outstanding requests. That is a gap in my information, not proof of secrecy. I have asked for clarification and the exact cottage for my fifteen o'clock tea appointment. I remain uneasy that something might be happening without my knowledge, but I have not observed concrete evidence of an unusual organized activity or established who would be involved or what it would be for.
